Container.Name: UnKeep
Container.Overview:
A private, self-hosted, Google Keep-style notes app with end-to-end encrypted sync. Notes are encrypted on your devices; this container only stores ciphertext. AI agents and scripts can use the same vault through the bundled unkeep CLI.
HTTPS is required: on plain HTTP (including the WebUI button) you'll see an "UnKeep needs HTTPS" page. Use Tailscale Serve, a reverse proxy, or Cloudflare Tunnel.
Set two different random tokens below (openssl rand -hex 32). On your first device, enter the setup token and save the recovery kit. Back up appdata before updating.
Container.Requires: HTTPS (Tailscale Serve, a reverse proxy, or Cloudflare Tunnel). Plain HTTP on the LAN does not work.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Web app port (plain HTTP). Put HTTPS in front of it; don't expose it to the internet directly.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Encrypted vault database. No preparation needed. Back it up before updating.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the app runs as. It takes ownership of the data folder on start. Must not be 0.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the app runs as. Must not be 0.

Config.Name: Setup token
Config.Description: Creates the vault on your first device. 32-256 characters, no spaces (openssl rand -hex 32).

Config.Name: Recovery token
Config.Description: Restores access with your recovery kit if you lose every device. Must differ from the setup token. Keep it safe.

Config.Name: Link previews
Config.Description: Set to 1 for Keep-style link previews. The server then sees previewed URLs and needs internet access.

Config.Name: Allowed origin
Config.Description: Only for a separately hosted web app: its exact origin, such as https://notes.example.com. Usually empty.

Config.Name: Trust proxy
Config.Description: Set to 1 only if your reverse proxy replaces X-Forwarded-For, so rate limits see real client addresses.

Config.Name: Max attachment size
Config.Description: Attachment limit in bytes, default 26214400 (25 MiB). Lower it to restrict uploads; the apps never send more than 25 MiB.
